concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx passes controller.signal to fetch and swallows err.name === 'AbortError' in the catch, rethrowing everything else, so a superseded request never calls onResults with stale data

concepts.name: URL Encoding
concepts.description: User text placed in a URL query string must be percent-encoded so reserved characters like & # and spaces do not change the URL's structure.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx builds /api/search?q= with encodeURIComponent(query) so input like 'a&b' stays inside the q parameter
SearchBox.tsx aborts the previous request in effect cleanup so a slow response for 'ab' cannot overwrite results for 'abc' via onResults
SearchBox.tsx lists [query, onResults]; if the parent passes an unmemoized onResults, every parent render re-runs the effect, resetting the debounce and aborting the request
SearchBox.tsx renders <input value={query} onChange={...setQuery}> so the query state drives the effect that fetches results

concepts.name: Effect Cleanup
concepts.description: A useEffect can return a cleanup function that React runs before the next effect run and on unmount. It is where timers, subscriptions and in-flight requests are cancelled so stale work never fires.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx returns a cleanup that calls clearTimeout(timer) and controller.abort(), so each keystroke cancels the previous pending debounce and in-flight fetch before the effect re-runs

concepts.name: Debounce
concepts.description: Delaying an action until input has been quiet for a set time, so rapid events (keystrokes) trigger one call instead of many.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx wraps the fetch in a 250ms setTimeout inside useEffect; changing query clears the timer, so only the last keystroke in a burst hits /api/search

concepts.name: Fetch Cancellation
concepts.description: AbortController gives fetch a signal; calling abort() rejects the request with an AbortError. It cancels in-flight requests and prevents out-of-order responses overwriting newer ones.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx passes controller.signal to fetch and the catch block ignores err.name === 'AbortError' but rethrows others, so a superseded search never calls onResults with stale data

concepts.name: useEffect Dependencies
concepts.description: useEffect re-runs when values in its dependency array change. Props used inside, such as callbacks, must be listed, and unstable identities cause extra re-runs.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx effect depends on [query, onResults]; if the parent passes an inline onResults function, its changing identity re-triggers the effect and restarts the debounce each render, so the parent should memoize it with useCallback

concepts.name: URL Encoding
concepts.description: User input placed in a URL query string must be percent-encoded so reserved characters like & # and spaces do not change the request's meaning.
concepts.context: SearchBox.tsx builds /api/search?q= with encodeURIComponent(query) so input like 'a&b=1' stays one parameter value
In SearchBox.tsx, the effect cleanup aborts the previous fetch, so only the latest query's response reaches onResults even if an earlier request would resolve later
SearchBox.tsx binds <input value={query} onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}> so the effect reacts to every keystroke through state

concepts.name: Conditional Requests
concepts.description: Validating a cached response with an ETag and If-None-Match so the server can answer 304 Not Modified without resending the body.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: hash the JSON catalog into a quoted ETag, compare to If-None-Match and return 304 with no body, saving bandwidth on unchanged catalogs

concepts.name: Stale While Revalidate
concepts.description: Cache-Control extension that lets a cache serve a stale response for a window while it refreshes in the background, trading freshness for latency.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: max-age=60 plus stale-while-revalidate=300 lets clients and CDNs reuse the catalog up to 5 minutes past expiry while revalidating

concepts.name: Vary Header
concepts.description: The Vary response header names request headers that change the response, so shared caches key stored copies on them and don't serve the wrong variant.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: Vary: Accept-Language so a CDN does not serve one locale's catalog to a user requesting another

concepts.name: Content-Hash ETag
concepts.description: Deriving a strong ETag from a hash of the serialized body, so the validator changes exactly when the content does; costs a full load and serialize per request.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: etag is hash(JSON.stringify(catalog)) computed after loadCatalog(), so 304s save bandwidth but not server work

etag-conditional-requests.why: The code sets a quoted ETag and returns 304 on If-None-Match match, and the context states that behavior.

stale-while-revalidate.why: The Cache-Control line sets stale-while-revalidate=300, and the context names the exact value and its 5-minute effect.

vary-header.why: The code sets Vary: Accept-Language, and the context explains why: to avoid cross-language cache mixups.

public-shared-cache.why: The 'public' directive is in the code, and the context gives the reason it is safe: the catalog is not user-specific.

content-hash-etag.why: The ETag is hashed from the serialized catalog, and the context notes that a 304 still pays the load and serialize cost.

concepts.name: ETag revalidation
concepts.description: Validator-based caching: the server sends an ETag, the client replays it in If-None-Match, and an equal value gets a bodyless 304 Not Modified instead of the full payload.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: hashes the JSON catalog into a quoted ETag and returns 304 when If-None-Match equals it, so unchanged catalogs skip the body

concepts.name: Stale-while-revalidate
concepts.description: Cache-Control extension letting a cache serve a stale response for a set window while it refetches in the background, trading brief staleness for latency.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: Cache-Control 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300' lets caches serve a catalog up to 5 minutes past expiry while revalidating

concepts.name: Vary header
concepts.description: Vary names the request headers that change the response, so shared caches key stored copies on them and don't serve one variant to a client who needs another.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: Vary 'Accept-Language' keeps CDN and browser caches from serving one language's catalog to another language's client

concepts.name: Shared cache scope
concepts.description: The 'public' directive lets shared caches such as CDNs store a response, not only the browser, so it must only be used for content identical across users.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: 'public' on /catalog allows CDN storage, safe only because the catalog is not user-specific and varies only by language

concepts.name: Content-hash ETag
concepts.description: Deriving an ETag by hashing the serialized response body gives a stable validator tied to content, at the cost of building the body on every request before comparing.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: etag is hash(JSON.stringify(catalog)) after loadCatalog(), so a 304 still pays for loading and serializing the catalog; only the response body is saved

http-etag-conditional-requests.why: Code hashes catalog into ETag and returns 304 on If-None-Match match; context notes the hash is computed after loading so only bandwidth is saved.

stale-while-revalidate.why: Cache-Control sets max-age=60 and stale-while-revalidate=300, and the context explains the resulting 6-minute staleness window.

http-vary-header.why: Vary: Accept-Language is set and the context explains the CDN purpose; the ETag claim is a bit speculative since the code doesn't show language-specific loading.

public-shared-cache-directive.why: Cache-Control includes public, and the context explains why that's safe for a shared catalog versus private for per-user data.

http-status-codes.why: The handler returns 304 with an early return so it doesn't fall through to res.json, and the context says so.

concepts.name: ETag revalidation
concepts.description: Validating a cached response with a strong ETag and If-None-Match, so the server can answer 304 Not Modified with no body when the representation has not changed.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: hashed the JSON catalog into a quoted ETag and returned 304 when If-None-Match matched, so unchanged catalogs skip the body. The hash is computed after loadCatalog() runs, so the server still does the work and only the bandwidth is saved.

concepts.name: Stale-while-revalidate
concepts.description: A Cache-Control extension that lets a cache serve an expired response for a set window while it refetches a fresh one in the background, trading some freshness for lower latency.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: set max-age=60 plus stale-while-revalidate=300, so a client may show a catalog up to 6 minutes old (60s fresh plus 300s stale) while a refresh runs behind it.

concepts.name: Vary header
concepts.description: The Vary response header names the request headers that change the response, so shared caches keep a separate entry per value and do not serve one variant to the wrong client.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: Vary: Accept-Language, so a CDN does not serve the English catalog to a French-speaking client. The ETag is built from the catalog body, so each language gets its own validator.

concepts.name: Public cache directive
concepts.description: Cache-Control: public allows shared caches such as CDNs and proxies to store a response, not just the browser. Combined with a per-user response it can leak data between users.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: marked the route public so a CDN can hold the catalog. That is safe only because the catalog is the same for every user, apart from language. Per-user data here would need private.

concepts.name: HTTP status codes
concepts.description: The meaning of response status classes and codes, including 304 Not Modified, which tells a client to reuse its cached copy and carries no body.
concepts.context: catalog.ts: ended the response early with res.status(304).end() and a return when the validator matched, so the handler never falls through to res.json(catalog).
